steps.say: What does Postgres hosting cost on Supabase, Neon and Railway?
steps.text:
All three have a $0 free tier. The cheapest paid entry is Railway Hobby at $5/month [2][3]. Neon's Launch plan is usage-based with a typical spend of $15/month [1]. Supabase Pro starts at $25/month [4][7][8]. **None of these sources shows a date**, so check the official pricing pages before you commit.

| Provider | Free | Entry paid | Higher tiers | Usage rates |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Supabase** | $0 [4] | Pro: $25 per organization/month plus usage [8] | Team: $599/month; Enterprise: custom [4] | Not in sources |
| **Neon** | $0, no credit card [1] | Launch: usage-based, typical spend $15/month [1] | Scale (price not shown) | Compute: $0.106/CU-hour on Launch, $0.222/CU-hour on Scale [5] |
| **Railway** | $0 with $1/month usage credits [2] | Hobby: $5/month incl. $5 usage credits [2][3] | Pro: $20/month per workspace incl. $20 credits [2][3]; Enterprise: custom [3] | RAM $10/GB/month [3][6]; CPU $20/vCPU/month [3][6]; egress $0.05/GB [3] |

**How the billing models differ:**
- **Supabase** charges a flat fee per organization, plus usage on top [8].
- **Neon** charges for compute hours, so the bill depends on how long your database runs.
- **Railway** has no Postgres-specific plan. You pay for the CPU, RAM and egress your database container uses. The monthly credits offset those charges [2][3].

**Source reliability:**
- **Railway** is well supported. Its numbers come from Railway's own pricing pages [2][3] and match a third-party source [6].
- **Supabase** has no official pricing page in these sources. The $25 Pro price is consistent across three third-party pages [4][7][8], but the $599 Team price is **single-sourced** [4]. Confirm both at supabase.com/pricing.
- **Neon**'s CU-hour rates are **single-sourced** from a third-party blog [5]. Neon's official page [1] here shows only the free plan and the $15 typical spend. Confirm the rates at neon.com/pricing.

The sources don't give storage or other per-unit rates for Supabase or Neon, so I can't estimate a full bill for those two.

steps.say: We're a 20-person sales team. Compare HubSpot, Pipedrive, Salesforce, Zoho CRM and Close pricing.
steps.text:
For 20 seats, the cheapest entry tiers are **Pipedrive Lite and Zoho CRM Standard, at about $280/month each**. Mid-tier plans from all five vendors cost roughly $460–$2,180/month. Most of these numbers come from undated third-party guides, so confirm them on the vendors' own pricing pages before you budget.

## Per-user prices and 20-seat monthly cost

| Vendor | Plan | Per user / month | 20 seats / month |
|---|---|---|---|
| HubSpot | Starter | $20 [6] | 20 x $20 [6] = $400 |
| HubSpot | Starter (new-customer offer, annual) | $7 [8] | 20 x $7 [8] = $140 |
| HubSpot | Professional | $1,300/mo flat with 6 seats [8] | Can't compute (extra-seat price not in sources) |
| Pipedrive | Lite | $14 annual / $24 monthly [9] | 20 x $14 [9] = $280 (annual) or 20 x $24 [9] = $480 (monthly) |
| Pipedrive | Premium | $49 [5] | 20 x $49 [5] = $980 |
| Pipedrive | Ultimate | $79 annual / $99 monthly [9] | 20 x $79 [9] = $1,580 (annual) |
| Salesforce | Starter Suite | $25 [10] | 20 x $25 [10] = $500 |
| Salesforce | Pro Suite | $100 [10] | 20 x $100 [10] = $2,000 |
| Salesforce | Enterprise (annual) | $165 [11] | 20 x $165 [11] = $3,300 |
| Zoho CRM | Standard | $14 [12] | 20 x $14 [12] = $280 |
| Zoho CRM | Professional | $23 [12] | 20 x $23 [12] = $460 |
| Zoho CRM | Enterprise | $40 [12] | 20 x $40 [12] = $800 |
| Zoho CRM | Ultimate | $52 [12] | 20 x $52 [12] = $1,040 |
| Close | Mid tier (monthly billing) | $49 [1] | 20 x $49 [1] = $980 |
| Close | Growth (monthly billing) | $109 [1] | 20 x $109 [1] = $2,180 |
| Close | Top tier (monthly billing) | $149 [1] | 20 x $149 [1] = $2,980 |

## Things to watch

- **Close:** Solo is $9/month but covers only one user, so it doesn't fit a team of 20 [1]. Its official page lists monthly prices of $19, $49, $109 and $149 [1]. A third-party guide instead gives $9–$139 per user per month on annual billing [4], so annual plans are likely cheaper.
- **HubSpot:** the sources disagree.
  - One guide puts Professional at $100–$890/month [6]. Another says it starts at $1,300/month with 6 seats included [8].
  - The $7 Starter price is a new-customer annual offer [8], not the standard rate.
  - HubSpot switched to seats-and-credits pricing in EMEA from October 2026, with Starter from €20 per seat [6]. The sources don't show how this applies in India.
- **Pipedrive** has no free plan, only a 14-day free trial [9]. Annual billing saves up to 42% compared with monthly [9]. Published prices run from $14 to $99 per user per month on annual billing [7].
- **Zoho** has a free plan for up to 3 users [12], which is too small for your team. One source gives the top "Plus" plan as $57 per user per month [3], separate from the Ultimate price above [12].
- **Billing basis is unclear for some rows.** The sources don't say whether the Zoho and Salesforce Starter/Pro figures are annual or monthly billing.

## Reliability (high-stakes check)

- Close's monthly prices are the only ones from an official page [1], and that page is undated.
- Almost every other figure is **single-sourced** from an undated third-party guide. The exception is Pipedrive's $14 Lite price, which two sources support [7][9].
- None of the sources show India (INR) pricing or taxes.

Before deciding, check each vendor's official pricing page for your region. Also ask Salesforce, HubSpot and Pipedrive for a 20-seat quote, since vendors often discount at that size.

What does idempotent mean?
steps.text:
**Idempotent means doing an operation once has the same effect as doing it many times.** After the first application, repeating it changes nothing further.

**In math:** f is idempotent if f(f(x)) = f(x).
- Absolute value: |(|−5|)| = |−5| = 5
- Rounding a number, or taking the max of a value with itself

**In programming and APIs:** a request is idempotent if sending it twice leaves the system in the same state as sending it once.
- `PUT /users/42 {name: "Asha"}` is idempotent. Setting the name to "Asha" again changes nothing.
- `DELETE /users/42` is idempotent. Once the user is deleted, it stays deleted, though a second call might return "not found."
- `POST /orders` usually is **not** idempotent. Each call may create a new order.

**Why it matters:** with idempotent operations, retries after timeouts or network errors are safe, because you can resend without fear of double charges or duplicate records. That's why payment APIs often accept an "idempotency key" so a repeated request is processed only once.

**Everyday analogy:** pressing an elevator call button. Pressing it five times doesn't summon five elevators.

steps.text:
Fly.io Managed Postgres starts at **$38/month (Basic plan) plus $0.28 per GB of storage per month** [5]. The official Fly.io pricing page shows no date. Third-party pages agree on these numbers [3][6], and one of them is labelled Sep 2026 [6].

## Plans

| Plan | Compute | Price/month |
|---|---|---|
| Basic | shared-2x, 1 GB RAM | $38 [5][6] |
| Starter | not stated | $72 [4] |
| Launch | not stated | $282 [4] |
| Scale | not stated | $962 [4] |
| Performance | performance-8x, 64 GB | $1,922 [5][6] |

- **Single-sourced:** Only one undated third-party blog gives the Starter, Launch and Scale prices [4]. The official page lists just the range from Basic to Performance [5].

- **Included:** Every plan includes high availability, backups and connection pooling [2]. Databases have no public internet access by design [1].

## Example costs

- **Small database with 10 GB storage:** $38 [5] + 10 GB x $0.28 [5] = $40.80 (unverified)/month. This matches the "about $41" figure in [2].
- **Small web app plus a Basic database:** Fly's own example comes to $43.67/month [5].

## Free trial

New accounts get $1 of credit, usable on Managed Postgres among other things. It lasts 7 days or until it's used up [5]. There is no ongoing free tier [7].

None of these sources are dated, and one mentions pricing changes on 1 October [4]. Before you commit, check the current figures at docs.fly.io/about/pricing.
